title: INDIA Bloc Seeks Supreme Court Nod to Put 48 Questions to Election Commission
excerpt: Opposition leaders want sworn, record-backed answers on whether the SIR decisions and the Commission's own affidavit were really approved unanimously.
body:
• INDIA bloc leaders led by Rahul Gandhi have asked the Supreme Court for permission to serve 48 written questions, called interrogatories, on the Election Commission of India over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
  • The questions target the Commission's claim of unanimity: whether Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi approved the Commission's October 26 counter-affidavit and the three SIR orders behind it.
  • The petitioners also seek records on any dissents, the added declaration on the online Form 6 page, state-wise voter exclusions and changes to the ECINET platform.
  • The Election Commission has maintained that all three SIR orders were approved unanimously and has denied unilateral decision-making. The Supreme Court hears the matter on Tuesday, November 17.

Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders have filed an application in the Supreme Court seeking permission to serve 48 interrogatories on the Election Commission of India (ECI), including questions on whether the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners approved the counter-affidavit the Commission filed claiming that all decisions relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unanimously, according to Live Law.

The petitioners argue that the ECI's counter-affidavit, filed on October 26, relies on assertions of unanimous decisions and approvals without disclosing the corresponding dates, file notings, records or details of the decision-making process. Apart from Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, the petitioners include Saugata Roy, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, Sanjay Raut, M.A. Baby, D. Raja, Mahua Majhi, Supriya Sule and E.T. Muhammed Basheer, with two more opposition leaders later joining the petition. The application has been filed through advocate-on-record Prasanna S.

What the 48 questions ask

One set of questions goes to the affidavit itself. The petitioners have asked whether the affidavit filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu was approved by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and whether that approval was given at a meeting, through circulation of a file or by electronic communication. They want the relevant dates and records, and whether any member suggested modifications or expressed reservations.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xYNgLtOX5gE

"Approved for filing before this Hon'ble Court by a unanimous decision of the three members of the Election Commission."

— Election Commission of India, counter-affidavit of October 26, as reported by Live Law

A second set seeks details of any objections, dissents or reservations the Election Commissioners recorded in writing between February 19, 2025 and October 26, 2026 on SIR decisions, ECINET, Form 6 and the filing of appeals, and how many occasions there were. A September report by The Indian Express had identified 14 instances in which the two commissioners reportedly recorded objections or concerns, as noted in coverage of the filing.

A third set concerns the SIR orders dated June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025 and May 14, 2026. The petitioners seek the file numbers, dates and manner of each decision, and the dates each member signified approval. They also point to an apparent discrepancy: an order of the Commission's First Appellate Authority under the Right to Information Act reportedly stated that the Commission had not taken a decision to initiate a nationwide SIR in 2025.

Form 6, deletions and the ECINET system

The application also seeks details about the addition of a declaration to the online Form 6 application page, including who introduced it, when it was done and whether the decision was approved by the Commission. Form 6 is the form citizens use to apply for inclusion in the electoral rolls. The petitioners ask how many Form 6 applications were submitted, rejected, kept pending or left unprocessed because of the declaration or mapping-related requirements.

They have sought state-wise data on electors excluded from draft or final rolls, with reasons such as death, shifting, absence, duplication or ineligibility. Other questions cover Form 7 objections, whether any roll entry was changed other than on a registration officer's order, whether ECINET let officers restore a deleted entry, and whether Dr. Vivek Joshi's proposal for an audit of database access was placed before the Commission.

The Commission's position

In its counter-affidavit filed on October 26, the ECI maintained that the three SIR orders were unanimously approved by all three members of the Commission. It denied that the Chief Election Commissioner had taken unilateral decisions on the SIR, and maintained that the additional declaration required during the exercise did not amount to an amendment of statutory Form 6.

What happens next

The Supreme Court issued notice in the underlying proceedings on October 15, gave the petitioners 10 days to respond to the Commission's affidavit, and hears the matter on November 17, before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. If the court allows the application, the Commission's senior officials would have to answer the 48 questions on affidavit, supported by records.
